subject: Learning Methods
title: Deep Sleep and Fact Memory
description: A quick win: understand Deep Sleep and Fact Memory.

hook.text: Deep Sleep and Fact Memory: effective learning usually works differently from what feels easiest.

buildup.text: Deep sleep, also called slow-wave sleep, produces long, slow brain oscillations.

discovery.text: The hippocampus replays experiences during deep sleep like a recording. This replay strengthens neural connections.

twist.text: Deep Sleep and Fact Memory shows that effective learning often feels harder in the moment.

climax.text: To maximize deep sleep for fact learning, go to bed early enough to capture the first half of the night fully.

punchline.text: Early sleep is deep sleep. Early bedtimes protect fact memory.

quiz.question: When does most deep sleep occur during the night?
options: Concentrated in the first half of the night
Only in the final two hours before waking
